The encoding phase prepares a compressed, temporally coherent data structure [S1, S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the encoding phase prepares a compressed, temporally coherent data structure. The evidence from Source [S1] explicitly describes the process: 'A compression and rendering technique... that uses octree structures to encode differences between time steps' and 'By exploiting spatial and temporal coherence in the data... two subtrees at consecutive time steps may be merged if they are identical.' This confirms that the encoding creates a compressed structure (via quantization and octree-difference encoding) that leverages temporal coherence (merging identical subtrees across time steps).

Gain:** Datasets with many small matching blocks and few large matching blocks (e.g., turbulent shear flow with non-uniform quantization) incur overhead from the octree structure that exceeds the gains from compression, leading to slower rendering than baseline [S1, S2, unofficial].

The claim is explicitly supported by the text in both Source [S1] and Source [S2]. Both sources contain the exact statement: 'datasets which have many small matching blocks and few large matching blocks typically require more overhead to use the octree than can be gained by using the compression information,' and specifically cite 'turbulent shear dataset' (or 'turbulent shear flow') as an example where this occurs, leading to slower rendering or increased rendering time compared to cases with large blocks.
